questions.question: Which was the new scheme announced during Budget 2025-26 that targets 100 low productivity districts and focuses on enhancing agricultural productivity, crop diversification, sustainable practices, irrigation and post-harvest storage?

• The scheme also promotes the adoption of climate-resilient farming practices to ensure long-term sustainability in agricultural activities.

• **Irrigation Infrastructure:** Proper irrigation systems help in water management for farming, ensuring that crops receive adequate water during critical growth periods.
 
• **Post-Harvest Management:** This includes activities such as storage, processing, and transportation of crops to prevent spoilage and improve marketability.
 
• **Climate-Resilient Farming:** These are agricultural methods designed to withstand the adverse effects of climate change, such as drought-tolerant crops and water-conservation techniques.

questions.question: Which of the following is not one of the Ettuttokai (Eight Anthologies) of the Sangam literature?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tolkappiyam**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Ettuttokai**, or the Eight Anthologies, is a collection of classical Tamil Sangam literature consisting of eight works of poetry.
 
• The Eight Anthologies are: **Purananuru, Kuruntokai, Narrinai, Aingurunuru, Kalittokai, Paripadal, Padirruppattu, and Akananuru**.
 
• **Tolkappiyam** is not part of the Ettuttokai; it is a separate work considered the earliest Tamil grammar text and one of the oldest surviving works in Tamil literature.
 
• The Ettuttokai primarily focuses on themes of love (akam) and war (puram), reflecting the socio-cultural aspects of Tamil life during the Sangam era.
 
• The Sangam literature is an invaluable resource for understanding the early history, culture, and language of Tamil Nadu.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sangam Literature:** Sangam literature refers to the ancient Tamil literature created during the Sangam period, spanning approximately 300 BCE to 300 CE.
 
• **Tolkappiyam:** This is a comprehensive work on Tamil grammar, phonetics, morphology, and syntax, written by the scholar Tolkappiyar.
 
• **Akam and Puram:** Akam refers to inner (love and personal) themes, while Puram pertains to outer (war and public life) themes in Sangam poetry.
 
• **Other Sangam Works:** Apart from Ettuttokai, the Sangam corpus includes Pattuppāṭṭu (Ten Idylls) and other standalone works.
 
• **Historical Significance:** Sangam texts provide insights into the societal structure, governance, trade, and cultural practices of ancient Tamil Nadu.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of the .ppsx file format in MS PowerPoint 365?

options.text: To save the presentation in a format that opens directly in Slide Show mode
To save the presentation in a read-only format
To save the presentation as a template for future use
To compress the presentation file size

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**To save the presentation in a format that opens directly in Slide Show mode**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The .ppsx file format in MS PowerPoint is specifically designed to open presentations directly in **Slide Show mode**.
 
• It bypasses the editing interface, ensuring that viewers see the presentation in its intended display form.
 
• This format is commonly used for final presentations, where edits are no longer required, and the focus is on presenting.
 
• .ppsx files are part of the Office Open XML standard introduced with Microsoft Office 2007.
 
• It is a non-editable format unless explicitly opened in PowerPoint for editing.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **PowerPoint File Formats:**

 
 
• **.pptx:** Default editable format for PowerPoint presentations.
 
• **.potx:** Template file format used for creating new presentations with pre-defined designs.
 
• **.ppsx:** Slide Show format that opens directly for presentation purposes.
 
• **.ppt:** Legacy file format used in older versions of PowerPoint.
 
 
 
• **Slide Show Mode:** A mode in PowerPoint where the presentation is displayed as a sequence of slides for an audience.
 
• **Office Open XML Standard:** A set of file formats introduced in Microsoft Office 2007 that ensures cross-platform compatibility.
 
• **Benefits of .ppsx Format:**
 
 
• Ensures presentations are viewed as intended without accidental edits.
 
• Ideal for distributing final versions of presentations.
 
• Compatible with most modern versions of MS PowerPoint.
 
 
 
• **How to Create a .ppsx File:** Save your presentation in MS PowerPoint by selecting "Save As" and choosing the .ppsx format.

questions.question: Which Mauryan ruler sent Buddhist missionaries to foreign countries?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ashoka**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Ashoka the Great** (reigned c. 268–232 BCE) was one of the most prominent rulers of the Maurya Dynasty and is considered a key figure in the promotion of Buddhism worldwide.
 
• After the Kalinga War, Ashoka embraced Buddhism and adopted the policy of "Dhamma" (righteousness).
 
• He sent Buddhist missionaries to several countries, including Sri Lanka, Southeast Asia, Central Asia, and the Mediterranean regions, to spread the teachings of Buddha.
 
• One of the most notable missions was led by his son Mahendra and daughter Sanghamitra to Sri Lanka, which played a pivotal role in the spread of Theravāda Buddhism.
 
• Ashoka's efforts are documented in his rock and pillar edicts, which outline his dedication to Buddhism and non-violence.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Buddhist Missionaries:** Ashoka's emissaries included monks, scholars, and members of the royal family, who traveled far and wide to propagate Buddhist teachings.
 
• **Kalinga War:** This war was a turning point in Ashoka's life; the immense bloodshed led him to renounce violence and adopt Buddhism as a guiding principle of governance.
 
• **Rock and Pillar Edicts:** Ashoka's inscriptions, written in Brahmi and other scripts, are some of the earliest examples of written records in India. They provide insights into his policies and commitment to Buddhism.
 
• **Dhamma Policy:** Ashoka's Dhamma was not limited to Buddhism but emphasized moral and ethical behavior, religious tolerance, and the welfare of all living beings.
 
• **Legacy:** Ashoka's efforts made Buddhism a major world religion, and he is remembered as one of history's most benevolent rulers.

questions.question: Which of the following statements best describes the role of RAM and ROM in a computer system?

options.text: RAM is used to store the operating system and permanent files, while ROM is used to store temporary data.
ROM is used for storing data that can be modified and written to, while RAM stores fixed data.
ROM is used to store system firmware, while RAM stores temporary data for active processes.
RAM is non-volatile, while ROM is volatile

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**ROM is used to store system firmware, while RAM stores temporary data for active processes**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **ROM (Read-Only Memory)** is a non-volatile memory that stores firmware, which includes the BIOS or UEFI needed for starting the computer system.
 
• **RAM (Random Access Memory)** is a volatile memory used to store temporary data required by active processes and running applications.
 
• Data in RAM is lost when the computer is powered off, whereas data in ROM remains intact irrespective of power status.
 
• ROM provides essential instructions for booting up the computer, while RAM enables multitasking and smooth execution of programs.
 
• Examples of ROM include EEPROM, PROM, and flash memory, while RAM is often categorized as DRAM or SRAM.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **ROM (Read-Only Memory):**

 
 
• It is non-volatile, meaning it retains data even when the power is turned off.
 
• ROM is mainly used for storing system firmware and permanent instructions required during the startup process.
 
• Examples include the BIOS/UEFI in computers and firmware in embedded systems.
 
 
 
• **RAM (Random Access Memory):**
 
 
• It is volatile, meaning data is lost when the power is turned off.
 
• RAM allows quick read/write operations and is used for temporary data storage during the execution of tasks.
 
• Types of RAM include DRAM (Dynamic RAM) and SRAM (Static RAM).
 
 
 
• **Firmware:**
 
 
• Firmware is a type of software embedded in hardware devices, stored in ROM.
 
• It provides low-level control and functionality to hardware components.
 
 
 
• **Volatile vs Non-Volatile Memory:**
 
 
• Volatile memory (e.g., RAM) requires power to maintain stored data.
 
• Non-volatile memory (e.g., ROM) retains data even after the power is turned off.

questions.question: 'Aus', 'Aman' and 'Boro' are important crops of which of the following in states like Assam, West Bengal and Odisha?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Paddy**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Aus, Aman, and Boro** are three major varieties of paddy grown in India, particularly in the eastern states like Assam, West Bengal, and Odisha.
 
• The cultivation of these varieties depends heavily on the **monsoon and water availability** for irrigation.
 
• **Aman** paddy is sown during the monsoon season (June-July) and harvested in winter (November-December).
 
• **Aus** paddy is cultivated during the pre-monsoon season and harvested before the onset of the monsoon.
 
• **Boro** paddy is grown during the dry season (November to May) using irrigation facilities, making it a winter crop.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Terminology:** Paddy refers to rice in its raw, unprocessed form, which is grown as a staple food crop in many parts of India.
 
• **Climatic Requirements:** Paddy requires a hot and humid climate, with temperatures ranging between 20°C to 35°C and a minimum of 100 cm of annual rainfall.
 
• **Geographical Importance:** Assam, West Bengal, and Odisha are among the largest producers of paddy in India due to their fertile soil and favorable climatic conditions.
 
• **Economic Significance:** Paddy farming plays a crucial role in the agrarian economy of India, providing livelihood to millions of farmers and contributing significantly to food security.
 
• **Green Revolution Impact:** The introduction of high-yielding rice varieties during the Green Revolution significantly boosted paddy production in India.

questions.question: In which Indian state are the Kachchh and Kathiawar coasts located?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gujarat**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Kachchh (Kutch) and Kathiawar coasts are located in the state of **Gujarat**, India.
 
• Kachchh is known for its unique geographical features, including the **Rann of Kutch**, which is a salt marsh.
 
• The Kathiawar Peninsula, located in Gujarat, is bordered by the Arabian Sea and is home to **the Gir National Park**, the last refuge of the Asiatic lions.
 
• These coasts are significant for their **marine biodiversity, salt production, and mangrove ecosystems**.
 
• Both regions are key contributors to Gujarat's economy through industries like salt manufacturing, agriculture, and tourism.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kachchh Region:**

 
 
• The Rann of Kutch is divided into two parts—**Great Rann** and **Little Rann**.
 
• The area experiences extreme climate conditions, with hot summers and cold winters.
 
• The region is famous for its annual festival, the **Rann Utsav**, which showcases local art, culture, and heritage.
 
 
 
• **Kathiawar Peninsula:**
 
 
• It is bounded by the Arabian Sea to the west and south, the Gulf of Kutch to the northwest, and the Gulf of Khambhat to the southeast.
 
• It is rich in historical sites, including the ancient city of **Dwarka**, a significant pilgrimage site in Hindu mythology.
 
• The region is home to the Gir Forest, which is the only natural habitat of the **Asiatic lion**.
 
 
 
• **Economic Importance:**
 
 
• Gujarat is one of the largest producers of salt in India, with the Kutch region being a major contributor.
 
• The coastal areas support industries such as **fishing, shipbuilding, and petrochemicals**.
 
 
 
• **Environmental Significance:**
 
 
• The coastal areas are home to extensive **mangrove forests**, which act as natural barriers against coastal erosion.
 
• These regions are part of the **Global Biodiversity Hotspots** and are crucial for migratory birds and marine species.

questions.question: Which vitamin deficiency is most likely in a person with a blocked bile duct?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Vitamin A**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• A blocked bile duct impairs the absorption of fat-soluble vitamins, which include **Vitamins A, D, E, and K**.
 
• Vitamin A deficiency is more likely as it is a fat-soluble vitamin requiring bile for proper absorption.
 
• Vitamin A plays a crucial role in maintaining healthy vision, immune function, and skin integrity.
 
• A lack of bile prevents the emulsification of dietary fats, thereby reducing the bioavailability of fat-soluble vitamins like Vitamin A.
 
• Symptoms of Vitamin A deficiency include night blindness, dry eyes (xerophthalmia), and increased susceptibility to infections.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bile Duct Function:** The bile duct transports bile, which is essential for the digestion and absorption of dietary fats and fat-soluble vitamins.
 
• **Fat-Soluble Vitamins:** These include Vitamins A, D, E, and K, which are stored in the liver and fatty tissues and are absorbed along with dietary fats.
 
• **Vitamin A Sources:** Dietary sources include liver, fish oils, dairy products, and colorful fruits and vegetables (e.g., carrots, spinach, and sweet potatoes).
 
• **Other Fat-Soluble Vitamin Deficiencies:** A blocked bile duct can also lead to deficiencies in Vitamins D (affecting bone health), E (antioxidant function), and K (blood clotting).
 
• **Clinical Management:** Patients with bile duct obstruction may require supplementation of fat-soluble vitamins in water-soluble forms to prevent deficiencies.

questions.question: Which component is commonly used in a circuit to vary the resistance?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rheostat**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• A **rheostat** is a variable resistor used in electrical circuits to adjust the resistance.
 
• It is commonly used to control the flow of current in a circuit and thus regulate voltage or power.
 
• Rheostats are constructed with a resistive wire wound around an insulating core, allowing for resistance adjustment by moving a slider or wiper.
 
• They are widely utilized in applications such as dimming lights, controlling motor speed, and tuning radios.
 
• Unlike fixed resistors, rheostats offer the flexibility of altering resistance dynamically during operation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Resistor:** A passive electrical component that provides resistance to control current in a circuit. Fixed resistors have a set resistance value, unlike variable resistors like rheostats.
 
• **Potentiometer:** Another variable resistor, similar to a rheostat but typically used for measuring or dividing voltage rather than controlling current directly.
 
• **Ohm’s Law:** The fundamental principle governing the relationship between voltage (V), current (I), and resistance (R) in an electrical circuit, represented by the equation V = IR.
 
• **Applications of Rheostats:** Besides light dimming and motor control, rheostats are used in experimental setups to test circuits and components under varying resistance conditions.
 
• **Difference Between Rheostat and Transformer:** While a rheostat alters resistance to control current, a transformer is an electrical device that changes voltage levels through electromagnetic induction.

questions.question: Disinvestment proceeds contribute to non-tax revenue of the government. Which body manages disinvestment in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**DIPAM**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Department of Investment and Public Asset Management (DIPAM)** is the nodal agency in India for managing disinvestment and strategic sale of public sector enterprises (PSEs).
 
• DIPAM operates under the **Ministry of Finance** and is responsible for generating revenue through the sale of government stakes in public sector companies.
 
• The department was earlier known as the **Department of Disinvestment** before being renamed as DIPAM in 2016.
 
• DIPAM's objective is to ensure optimal realization from the sale of government equity in central public sector enterprises (CPSEs).
 
• It also oversees the management of assets of public sector enterprises, including those earmarked for disinvestment.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Disinvestment:**

 
 
• It refers to the process of selling or liquidating the government’s stake in public sector undertakings (PSUs).
 
• The primary objective of disinvestment is to raise resources for the government and improve the operational efficiency of PSUs.
 
• Disinvestment proceeds are part of the non-tax revenue of the government.
 
 
 
• **Strategic Disinvestment:**
 
 
• It involves the sale of substantial portions of government equity in a PSU, often to private entities, along with the transfer of management control.
 
• Strategic disinvestment aims to bring in private sector expertise and investment for better management and growth of PSUs.
 
 
 
• **DIPAM’s Key Functions:**
 
 
• Formulating policies related to disinvestment and asset monetization.
 
• Advising the government on the timing and mode of disinvestment.
 
• Overseeing the listing of CPSEs on stock exchanges to unlock their value.
 
 
 
• **Examples of Recent Disinvestments:**
 
 
• Major disinvestment cases include the strategic sale of Air India, LIC IPO, and BPCL disinvestment.
 
• These initiatives aim to bridge the fiscal deficit and promote a self-reliant India.

questions.question: Which animal/bird was commonly depicted on Harappan seals?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Unicorn**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Unicorn** is one of the most commonly depicted motifs on Harappan seals, symbolizing a distinct cultural representation.
 
• Harappan seals were primarily made of **steatite**, a soft stone, and often featured intricate carvings of animals and other symbols.
 
• The Unicorn motif is unique to the Indus Valley Civilization and has not been found in other contemporary civilizations, showcasing its cultural exclusivity.
 
• Seals featuring the Unicorn were likely used for **trade and administrative purposes**, as they often included inscriptions in the undeciphered Harappan script.
 
• While the exact significance of the Unicorn remains unclear, it is hypothesized to represent a mythical or symbolic creature important to the Harappan people.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Harappan Seals:**

 
 
• Seals were primarily used for **identification, trade, and authentication**.
 
• They often featured animals like bulls, elephants, tigers, and mythical creatures like the Unicorn.
 
• Many seals included inscriptions in the **Harappan script**, which remains undeciphered to date.
 
 
 
• **Steatite Material:**
 
 
• Steatite was commonly used to make seals due to its **softness and ease of carving**.
 
• After carving, the seals were often fired to harden the material.
 
 
 
• **Trade Importance:**
 
 
• Harappan seals were integral to **trade networks** within the civilization and with Mesopotamia.
 
• They served as markers of ownership and authenticity for goods.
 
 
 
• **Unicorn Symbolism:**
 
 
• The Unicorn could represent a mythical or divine creature, central to Harappan beliefs.
 
• Its frequent appearance on seals suggests it held **significant cultural or religious importance**.

questions.question: During which phase and year was a steady population growth rate observed in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Phase II: 1921-1951**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The period from **1921 to 1951** is classified as Phase II in India's demographic history.
 
• During this phase, India saw a steady growth in its population due to improvements in **healthcare and sanitation**.
 
• This phase marked the beginning of a decline in mortality rates, although **birth rates remained high**.
 
• The steady population growth can be attributed to **better control of epidemics**, availability of vaccines, and improved public health measures.
 
• Phase II is often referred to as the "early expanding stage" in the demographic transition model.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Demographic Transition Model (DTM):** It explains the transition of countries from high birth and death rates to low birth and death rates through economic and social development.
 
• **Phase I (1891-1921):** Known as the "stagnant stage," India experienced very low population growth due to high mortality rates caused by famines, epidemics, and poor healthcare.
 
• **Phase III (1951-1981):** Characterized by rapid population growth due to a significant decline in death rates while birth rates remained high.
 
• **Phase IV (1981-2011):** Marked by a slowing population growth rate as birth rates began to decline due to family planning and increased literacy.
 
• **Factors Leading to Population Growth:** Economic development, improved medical facilities, access to education, and better hygiene practices are key contributors to population changes over time.

questions.question: Who among the following appoints the Chairman of the National Human Rights Commission of India?

options.text: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The President of India**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Chairman of the National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) of India is appointed by the **President of India**.
 
• The appointment is made based on the recommendations of a **high-level committee** constituted for this purpose.
 
• The high-level committee includes the Prime Minister, the Speaker of the Lok Sabha, the Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha, the Leaders of the Opposition in both Houses, and the Union Home Minister.
 
• As per the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993, the Chairman of NHRC is a retired Chief Justice of India or a judge of the Supreme Court.
 
• The NHRC is an independent statutory body, and the President's appointment ensures its functional autonomy.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a category of judicial review, as classified by Justice Syed Shah Mohammed Quadri?

options.text: Judicial review of administrative action of the Union and State and authorities under the state
Judicial review of judicial appointments to the Supreme Court and High Courts
Judicial review of legislation of the Parliament and State Legislatures and subordinate legislations

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Judicial review of judicial appointments to the Supreme Court and High Courts**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Judicial review refers to the power of the judiciary to examine the constitutionality of legislative acts, executive orders, and other governmental actions.
 
• Justice Syed Shah Mohammed Quadri classified judicial review into three categories: **review of legislative action, executive/administrative action, and constitutional amendments**.
 
• The judicial review of judicial appointments to the Supreme Court and High Courts is **not considered a separate category of judicial review** under this classification.
 
• The appointments of judges to the higher judiciary are primarily governed by the "Collegium System" and Articles 124 and 217 of the Indian Constitution, and their review is not a distinct judicial review category.
 
• Judicial review primarily focuses on safeguarding the Constitution and ensuring that no law or action violates fundamental rights.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Judicial Review of Legislative Action:** It involves examining laws passed by Parliament or State Legislatures to ensure their compliance with the Constitution.
 
• **Judicial Review of Administrative Action:** It ensures that administrative decisions by the executive or other authorities are not arbitrary, capricious, or unconstitutional.
 
• **Judicial Review of Constitutional Amendments:** The judiciary reviews amendments to ensure they do not violate the "basic structure" of the Constitution, as established in the landmark Kesavananda Bharati case (1973).
 
• **Collegium System:** It is a mechanism for appointing judges to the higher judiciary in India, involving the Chief Justice of India and senior judges of the Supreme Court.
 
• **Basic Structure Doctrine:** This doctrine ensures that certain fundamental principles of the Constitution cannot be altered, even by constitutional amendments.

• **Judicial Reforms:** The Act was part of broader legal reforms aimed at streamlining the judicial system in British India, ensuring uniformity and efficiency.

• During Mendeleev's time (late 19th century), the periodic table was incomplete, and many elements were yet to be discovered.
 
• **Radon** (Rn) is a noble gas discovered much later in 1900 by Friedrich Ernst Dorn. It was absent from Mendeleev's periodic table.
 
• **Polonium** (Po) was discovered in 1898 by Marie and Pierre Curie, a few decades after Mendeleev's initial work on the periodic table.
 
• Mendeleev left gaps in his periodic table for elements he predicted but had not yet been discovered. Radon and Polonium were not among the elements he predicted.
 
• In contrast, elements like Hydrogen, Nitrogen, Chlorine, and Fluorine were well-known during Mendeleev's time and incorporated into his periodic table.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mendeleev's Periodic Table**:

 
 
• Proposed in 1869 by Dmitri Mendeleev, it was based on atomic mass and properties of elements.
 
• He left gaps for elements that were not discovered yet, predicting their properties with remarkable accuracy.
 
• Gallium (discovered in 1875) and Germanium (discovered in 1886) were among the elements predicted by Mendeleev.
 
 
 
• **Noble Gases**:
 
 
• Noble gases like Radon were not part of Mendeleev's table because they were discovered later and required the addition of a new group in the periodic table.
 
• The group of noble gases was added after the discovery of Helium and Argon in the late 19th century.
 
 
 
• **Polonium**:
 
 
• A radioactive element discovered by Marie and Pierre Curie in 1898 while studying pitchblende.
 
• It was named after Poland, Marie Curie's homeland.
 
 
 
• **Radon**:
 
 
• Radon is a radioactive noble gas, discovered as a decay product of radium.
 
• It is colorless, odorless, and chemically inert, making its detection challenging initially.
 
 
 
• **Modern Periodic Table**:
 
 
• Organized by atomic number rather than atomic mass, as proposed by Henry Moseley in 1913.
 
• This resolved inconsistencies in Mendeleev's table, especially for elements like Argon and Potassium.

questions.question: What was the unemployment rate in India as per the Periodic Labour Force Survey during January to December 2024?

__
 
• The unemployment rate in India during January to December 2024 was recorded at **3.2%** according to the Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS).
 
• This figure represents a **decrease in unemployment rates** compared to previous years, indicating an improvement in the labor market.
 
• The PLFS, conducted by the **National Statistical Office (NSO)**, is the key survey for tracking unemployment and labor force participation in India.
 
• Rural unemployment stood at a **lower level** compared to urban areas, reflecting the differences in employment opportunities in these regions.
 
• The survey highlights a **rise in self-employment** and informal sector jobs, contributing to the decline in the unemployment rate.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS):**

 
 
• Launched by the NSO in 2017, PLFS is India’s official household-based employment survey.
 
• It provides data on key labor market indicators like unemployment, workforce participation, and labor force participation rates.
 
 
 
• **Unemployment Rate:**
 
 
• Defined as the percentage of people in the labor force who are unemployed and actively seeking employment.
 
• This is a key indicator of economic health and labor market conditions.
 
 
 
• **Urban vs Rural Employment:**
 
 
• Urban areas typically see higher unemployment rates due to reliance on formal sector jobs.
 
• Rural areas often have lower rates due to the prevalence of agricultural and informal work.
 
 
 
• **Labor Force Participation Rate (LFPR):**
 
 
• The proportion of the population aged 15 years and above that is either working or actively seeking work.
 
• India’s LFPR has historically been lower than global averages, especially for women.
 
 
 
• **Self-Employment in India:**
 
 
• A significant portion of India’s workforce is engaged in self-employment, particularly in agriculture, trade, and small-scale industries.
 
• Self-employment contributes to reducing unemployment but often involves low-income and unstructured work.

questions.question: What power does the President of India hold regarding the Contingency Fund of India?

options.text: The President approves the annual disbursement of the fund.
The President controls the fund to advance money for unforeseen expenses.
The President can only advise on the use of the fund.
The President delegates the control of the fund to the Finance Commission.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The President controls the fund to advance money for unforeseen expenses**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Contingency Fund of India is established under Article 267 of the Indian Constitution.
 
• The President of India has the authority to control the Contingency Fund and advance money for unforeseen or urgent expenditure.
 
• The fund is operated by the Secretary to the Government of India in the Ministry of Finance, under the President's authority.
 
• This fund is utilized for expenditures that cannot wait for parliamentary approval due to the urgent nature of the situation.
 
• Once the expenditure is incurred, it is subsequently regularized by obtaining parliamentary approval through the presentation of a Supplementary Budget.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Amount Allocated:** The Contingency Fund of India currently has a corpus of Rs. 500 crore, which can be increased if necessary.
 
• **Regularization Process:** Expenditure from the fund must be approved by Parliament retrospectively to ensure accountability.
 
• **State-Level Contingency Funds:** Similar funds exist at the state level, where the Governor exercises control over the fund.
 
• **Ministry of Finance's Role:** The fund is managed by the Ministry of Finance, ensuring efficient and transparent utilization of resources.

questions.question: The subtropical jet stream plays a critical role in the withdrawal of the monsoon by which of the following?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Inducing subsidence over land**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The subtropical jet stream shifts southward during the monsoon withdrawal phase, causing a **high-pressure system to develop over land**.
 
• This high-pressure system leads to **subsidence (downward movement of air)**, which suppresses convection and reduces rainfall.
 
• Subsidence over land promotes the **replacement of moist monsoonal winds with dry winds**, marking the retreat of the monsoon.
 
• The subtropical jet stream plays a pivotal role by inducing large-scale atmospheric stability, halting further moisture advection from the oceans.
 
• As a result, the **Intertropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ)** shifts southward, coinciding with the monsoon withdrawal process.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Subtropical Jet Stream:**

 
 
• A high-altitude, fast-moving air current located around 30° latitude in both hemispheres.
 
• It plays a critical role in influencing weather patterns, including the onset and withdrawal of monsoons.
 
 
 
• **Intertropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ):**
 
 
• A low-pressure zone near the equator where trade winds converge, leading to upward motion and cloud formation.
 
• The ITCZ shifts seasonally, influencing monsoon dynamics.
 
 
 
• **Subsidence:**
 
 
• The downward movement of air in the atmosphere, which suppresses cloud formation and precipitation.
 
• Often associated with the presence of high-pressure systems.
 
 
 
• **Monsoon Withdrawal:**
 
 
• The retreat of monsoonal winds marked by decreasing rainfall and the establishment of dry continental air over the region.
 
• Typically begins in northwest India and progresses southeastward.
 
 
 
• **Cold Air Advection:**
 
 
• The horizontal movement of cooler air into a region, often associated with the strengthening of high-pressure systems.
 
• While cold air advection plays a role in weather changes, it is not directly responsible for monsoon withdrawal.

questions.question: What must State legislators do under Article 188 of the Constitution of India before taking their seats for the first time in state assembly?
questions.solution:

__
 
• Under Article 188 of the Indian Constitution, every member of the State Legislature is required to **take an oath or make an affirmation** before taking their seat in the State Assembly or Council.
 
• The oath or affirmation is administered by the **Governor of the state or a person appointed by the Governor**.
 
• The purpose of the oath is to ensure that legislators uphold the **integrity of the Constitution and discharge their duties faithfully.**
 
• A member cannot participate in the proceedings of the legislature or vote until they have taken the **prescribed oath or affirmation.**
 
• The format of the oath or affirmation is provided in the **Third Schedule** of the Indian Constitution.

• **Third Schedule:** It contains the prescribed forms of oaths or affirmations for various constitutional posts, including State Legislators.
 
• **Governor's Role:** The Governor, as the constitutional head of the state, is responsible for administering the oath or appointing someone to do so.
 
• **Consequences of Not Taking Oath:** A legislator who does not take the oath cannot participate in legislative proceedings, vote, or receive any privileges associated with their role.
 
• **Similar Provision for Parliament:** Article 99 of the Constitution provides a similar requirement for members of the Parliament to take an oath or affirmation before assuming their duties.

questions.question: When utilising the 'Paste Special' function in MS Word to insert content copied from a spreadsheet, which of the following paste options would preserve the original formula calculations while displaying the calculated values in the Word document?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**MS Excel Worksheet Object**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **'MS Excel Worksheet Object'** option allows content copied from a spreadsheet to be pasted into MS Word while retaining the original formula calculations.
 
• When pasted as an MS Excel Worksheet Object, the data remains editable within MS Word, and users can view or modify the formulas through Excel functionalities.
 
• This option ensures accurate representation of calculated values derived from formulas, making it ideal for financial, statistical, or computational data.
 
• Unlike other options such as 'Unformatted Text' or 'HTML Format,' this method maintains the dynamic link between Word and Excel, allowing updates to the content.
 
• It is particularly useful for integrating spreadsheet data into Word documents without losing the integrity of calculations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Paste Special Functionality:**

 
 
• Paste Special allows users to control how content is inserted into a document, offering options like formatting, linking, or embedding.
 
• It is accessible through the 'Home' tab or by right-clicking in MS Word or Excel.
 
 
 
• **Embedding vs Linking:**
 
 
• Embedding creates a static copy of the Excel content within Word, while linking dynamically updates the Word document when changes are made in Excel.
 
• The 'MS Excel Worksheet Object' option supports both embedding and linking, depending on user preferences.
 
 
 
• **Alternative Paste Options:**
 
 
• 'Picture (Enhanced Metafile)' converts the data into a non-editable image format.
 
• 'HTML Format' preserves basic web-style formatting but does not retain formulas.
 
• 'Unformatted Text' strips all formatting and formulas, leaving plain text.
 
 
 
• **Use Cases:**
 
 
• Ideal for reports, presentations, or documentation that requires the integration of calculated data from spreadsheets.
 
• Frequently used in professional fields like finance, data analysis, and academic research.
